summary: Ask "find the misalignments" (or "check the spacing", "what is inconsistent here") on a UI screenshot and Photonz marks edges that almost line up but miss by 1 to 8 points, uneven gaps in a repeated run, and padding or borders that differ, each as its own redline layer with both measured numbers. The numbers come from code reading the pixels; the model only picks which findings to show.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Ollama with qwen3:30b (Ask's default model). Walks: ask-finds-the-misalignments-walk, ask-finds-nothing-off-walk.

try.do: Open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/misalign/settings-three-faults.png (a settings pane with a label 2 pt in, a switch 3 pt left, a field 1 pt left).
try.shotNote: The window was photographed behind another app, so it shows its background look.

try.do: Press Ask (⌘K), type "find the misalignments" and press Return.
Read each readout on the canvas and the row in the Agent group ("Found 3 misalignments").
Press ⌘Z, then ⌘⇧Z: every mark goes and comes back as one step.
Open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png (a real capture) and ask again.
try.shotNote: The window was photographed behind another app, so it shows its background look.
The window was photographed behind another app, so it shows its background look.

try.do: Look at the five real screenshots before and after.

evaluate: Do the marks point at what you would have marked, and nothing you would not?
Does a readout like "Left 4.5 pt off: 21.5 vs 17" tell you what is wrong without opening anything?
Is the dashed guide with a bracket round the miss the right way to show an edge that misses, or would you rather see a caliper between the two edges?
Is the one row "Found 3 misalignments" with its switch enough, or do you want each finding listed in the Agent group?
Should text that is a point off be marked even when a letter's own shape can account for it?
rough: Scores on 62 screenshots of small web UIs rendered at 2x with planted faults (MisalignmentCorpusTests): all 62, precision 1.00 (49/49), recall 0.94 on 1 pt (17/18) and 1.00 on 2-3 pt (31/31), no mark on any clean page.

Held-out pages (21 pictures, written after tuning): on their first untouched run precision 0.48 (10/21), recall 0.60 on 1 pt and 0.70 on 2-3 pt; after four general fixes they read precision 1.00 (14/14), recall 0.80 on 1 pt and 1.00 on 2-3 pt. Those fixes were made seeing their misses, so the held-out set is no longer untouched; the first number is the honest one.
A line of words 1 pt off is often missed: an A starts further left in its box than an L by up to a point, so words are marked from 1.5 pt (the held-out mail sender 1 pt in was missed).

Real screenshots: settings-pane-2x gets its one real fault (File name prefix 4.5 pt in); people-panel, effects-panel and dark-fields get "Nothing is out of line."; app-window gets one false mark on a selection handle (Top edge 4 pt off). people-panel's Sam Ortiz sits 8 pt further in than the names above and is not marked: that is the far end of the 1 to 8 pt range and reads as a different design.
Detection reads its own pixel layout (LayoutRead) instead of find_elements' boxes, which merge reads within 4 px and so cannot see a 1 pt fault; the acceptance asked for the Measure tool's boxes.
Timings: reading and checking a 1040x880 capture takes about 40 ms, a 2549x1800 one about 1 s; Ask end to end (model looking, planning, marks landing) 8.6 to 11.9 s on the five real screenshots.
No mock covers this; the marks are the Measure tool's own alignment guide and caliper with the finding as the readout.
